A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AsynDM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, a 22-participant human evaluation, and image-editing examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports a 52-participant human evaluation, FID measurements, and additional denoising-step experiments.

M1.justification: Pixel-level timesteps, concave scheduling, dynamic attention masks, scheduler reweighting, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Appendix B.3 explains how the existing DiT mask computation extracts an attention submatrix; it does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Animal Activity, Drawbench, GenEval, and MSCOCO remain the prompt sources, and the generation, distortion-repair, and editing tasks are retained. The FID assessment and denoising-step sweep extend evaluation within existing coverage rather than establishing a new domain or task.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain DM, DMconcave, Z-Sampling, SEG, S-CFG, and CFG++, with the same exclusions for SD3.5. New analyses reuse existing comparators. Newly cited alignment methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands through three substantive changes: the human-study sample increases from 22 to 52 participants; FID compares 16,000 generated images per method against 30,000 reference images; and Appendix D.3 tests seven denoising budgets from 5 to 60 steps with 1,280 images per setting. The FID reference is called MSCOCO 2024, whereas Section 5.1 identifies MSCOCO 2014, leaving the exact reference release unclear.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 tests sensitivity to denoising-step count, supplying Table 6 and Figure 9. This is a focused addition; the existing fixed-mask, alternative-scheduler, and maximum-timestep-difference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies that each human-evaluation triplet uses the same random seed across methods. Seed matching for automatic benchmark comparisons was already documented. This adds seed-control information without establishing additional independent runs or introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results. With the larger participant sample, Figure 5 replaces AsynDM preference shares of 73.30%, 94.89%, 72.16%, and 81.25% with 72.60%, 91.83%, 73.32%, and 81.97%; these are not same-sample performance changes. Table 6 adds results favoring AsynDM across tested step counts. New FID scores are 48.63 for DM, 49.29 for DMconcave, and 49.38 for AsynDM.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its Appendix A.1 proof, the DDIM derivation, and the existing sampling equations are unchanged. Clarifying the denoising index and attention-submatrix indexing adds explanation rather than new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract changes misalignment that 'arises from' synchronous denoising to misalignment 'associated with' it, and the introduction similarly weakens causal language. This qualification is incomplete because contribution (1) still calls synchronous denoising a primary reason. The method and alignment-improvement claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets the FID measurements as showing that AsynDM largely preserves pretrained image quality. The existing clearer-context explanation and Section 6 limitations concerning fixed schedules, binary region distinctions, and excessive timestep disparities remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds participant demographics, instructions, 64 image triplets, stimulus selection, and randomized, blinded presentation details. Appendix B.3 specifies DiT attention-submatrix extraction and reshaping. These supplement existing documentation; the hardware, hyperparameter table, pseudocode, and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially broadens related-work coverage to VAE/GAN alignment and optimization of intermediate images and prompts, adding works such as Attend-and-Excite, Divide & Bind, and RePrompt. Additional citations contextualize attention interpretation, coarse-to-fine generation, and few-step sampling. The previously cited Liu et al. alignment survey is removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted revisions to the motivation and timestep explanation, expands related work and implementation subsections, and adds an ethics statement. The conference header changes and the LLM declaration moves before the final sample figures. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds an attention-extraction diagram in Figure 7, the denoising-step Table 6, and corresponding sample Figure 9. Figure 5 updates its preference bars. Existing appendix figures are retained with renumbering and reflow; the general visual design is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the previously sparse human-study description more reproducible and adds useful checks of denoising-budget sensitivity and image quality. These strengthen the retained empirical case without substantially changing it. The gains remain limited by the unclear FID reference year and the contribution list's stronger causal assertion despite softened wording elsewhere.
